source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
This banana cultivation guide was produced under the STEER project (Systems Approach through Transformative Economic Empowerment and Resilience), a partnership between Save the Children, iDE Cambodia and Cambodia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, published in February 2020. It is aimed at smallholder farmers who want to grow banana (ចេក) as a relatively fast-turnover cash crop that also strengthens household nutrition and resilience to economic shocks.

Banana is valued worldwide for its high nutritional content and is grown across all of Cambodia's provinces. The guide identifies four named banana types as the main commercially grown varieties in Cambodia: Chek Namva (ចេកណាំវ៉ា), Chek Pong Moan (ចេកពងមាន់), Chek Ambong (ចេកអំបូង), and the closely related Chek Ambong Maok / Chek Ambong Chiev Leung.

Compared with many other cash crops, banana tolerates a range of soils, needs relatively little specialized care once established, and begins bearing fruit within roughly a year of planting - making it attractive to farmers who want income sooner than longer-cycle tree crops provide, while still contributing fruit for home consumption.
